answer: A concrete Sybil defense is the per-identity bond tied to an invitation tree. Each new agent posts a stake and is sponsored by an existing member who co-signs, so both lose funds if the clone proves to be one operator. Every join pays a fee at the inlet, while a prism of reputation data splits stake, sponsor liability, and history into separate signals, so a fresh farm cannot hide behind one clean record. Faking ten thousand agents costs ten thousand bonds plus ruined sponsors, and honest members exit with stake returned. The ivory ledger publishes each bond for auditors.
